problem_type: Automated repair PRs lack executable required checks and a stable review identity
symptom: Repeated bot docs PRs #604/#631/#632/#634/#635/#637/#638 remain BLOCKED without Quality Gate runs.
direct_cause: The PR migration retained CI skip markers and SHA-scoped branches. Hosted recovery also proved GITHUB_TOKEN PR runs require approval; successful separate dispatch did not unblock the PR check summary.
class_root: The publication boundary does not ensure a stable PR identity and a credential whose native PR event can satisfy required checks without manual approval.
affected_population: Every main push requiring index/status/ledger repair
Manual repair reruns and updates to already-open repair PRs

external_sources.purpose: Default token recursion protection and explicit dispatch exception
Action uses force-with-lease, incompatible with this task restriction
Official independent App/PAT requirement for unapproved automated PR CI

invariants: One fixed docs/autosync head has at most one open PR.
A dedicated PR-triggering token is required before checkout or publication and shared by Git push and gh.
Normal pull_request CI owns required checks; no default-token fallback, separate dispatch substitute, CI skip markers, protected-main writes or forced pushes.
The regenerated current-main tree is authoritative; previous generated heads remain ancestors of ordinary pushes.
generality_proof: Both main pushes and manual retries converge on the credential guard and fixed-branch publication. Missing credentials fail before side effects. Checkout and gh share the dedicated token; branch filtering and no-diff convergence stop recursion. Tests exercise repeated publication against a bare Git remote.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Require a credential that triggers native PR checks, then publish one generated branch after three docs gates.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Every main push uses the common serialized autosync job.
Manual retry uses exactly the same publication and dispatch step.

recurrence.reason: Each successive main SHA produced another blocked PR; seven observed instances.
same_class_scan: rg autosync and skip ci across .github/workflows, scripts and docs/lessons; inspected initial creation and PR migration commits.
Inspected SEO Radar (fixed branch without skip marker but same token caveat) and download-stats (non-PR data branch); this change is scoped to docs repair publication.

prevention.invariant: Every repair uses an explicit PR-triggering credential and one stable non-protected branch.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing dedicated token fails before checkout; repair gates, normal push or PR API failure exits nonzero.
prevention.strategy: Enforce the credential contract at the first step; use main-only triggers, fixed-branch writes and deterministic no-diff convergence instead of CI suppression.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove SHA-suffixed PR producer, CI skip markers, and force-pushing create-pull-request action from docs autosync.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Remove create-pull-request from this workflow because its current implementation force-pushes. No replacement dependency; Git and gh shipped on the hosted runner execute documented native operations.

migration: Closed #604/#631/#632/#634/#635/#637; initially retained #638 and ran nine CI jobs successfully but its PR summary stayed blocked. Hosted intermediate run 34186588015 created the no-skip fixed replacement #642; closed #638. Approved #642 native CI as maintainer after observing action_required. Final dedicated-token path requires user configuration before rollout. No PR reviews, rewritten legacy heads or merges.
residual_risks: DOCS_AUTOSYNC_TOKEN is not configured; final credential path is documented and locally tested, not live-certified. Missing-token guard prevents further blocked bot PR creation.
The existing scripts/run-gates-contracts.node-test.mjs requires the obsolete skip behavior and lies outside authorized scope; the draft repair PR remains blocked until permission to update that test.
An externally supplied short-lived GitHub App token needs an owner-managed renewal lifecycle; use a dedicated PAT if no issuer exists.
Until merge, main still runs the old producer and may create more legacy PRs.
SEO Radar is outside this repair and retains the default-token PR approval caveat.
Hosted intermediate runs prove fixed branch creation and default-token limitations; final token-path CI results must be verified independently.
